title: Vascular Programs in Emerging and Re-Emerging RNA Virus Infections: Comparative Lessons from SARS-CoV-2, Flaviviruses, and Hantaviruses
abstract: Emerging and re-emerging RNA viruses frequently present with clinical phenotypes that extend beyond classical organ tropism and include vascular leakage, platelet dysregulation, coagulation imbalance, microvascular injury, and thromboinflammation. SARS-CoV-2, flaviviruses, and hantaviruses provide three complementary models of virus-induced vascular disease. This narrative review compares these viruses through a shared endothelial–coagulative framework and proposes four partially overlapping vascular programs: endothelial activation, endothelial barrier failure, coagulation activation, and platelet quantitative or qualitative dysfunction. These programs are intended as a conceptual synthesis of convergent clinical, pathological, and experimental evidence rather than as a quantitative classification system. The framework is used not only to organize known mechanisms, but also to generate testable predictions for cross-virus biomarker panels, organ-specific endothelial models, and phenotype-guided clinical studies. Severe COVID-19 illustrates inflammation-driven endothelial activation, platelet–leukocyte interactions, complement amplification, NETosis, and immunothrombosis. Within the flavivirus group, DENV is used as the principal model for systemic vascular leakage, thrombocytopenia, and hemorrhagic risk; selected non-dengue flaviviruses illustrate how shared endothelial, platelet, and coagulation modules are redirected toward placental dysfunction (ZIKV), neuroinvasion (WNV and JEV), or hepatic failure and coagulopathy (YFV). Hantavirus infections provide a distinctive model of capillary leak syndrome in which non-lytic endothelial infection, immune-mediated injury, and permeability signaling converge on renal and pulmonary microvascular beds. A comparative view suggests that thrombotic, hemorrhagic, and leaky phenotypes are not mutually exclusive categories, but different outcomes of overlapping vascular programs shaped by viral tropism, vascular-bed specialization, immune activation, and host susceptibility.

SARS-CoV-2, flaviviruses, and hantaviruses provide three complementary models of virus-induced vascular disease. This narrative review compares these viruses through a shared endothelial–coagulative framework and proposes four partially overlapping vascular programs: endothelial activation, endothelial barrier failure, coagulation activation, and platelet quantitative or qualitative dysfunction. These programs are intended as a conceptual synthesis of convergent clinical, pathological, and experimental evidence rather than as a quantitative classification system. The framework is used not only to organize known mechanisms, but also to generate testable predictions for cross-virus biomarker panels, organ-specific endothelial models, and phenotype-guided clinical studies. Severe COVID-19 illustrates inflammation-driven endothelial activation, platelet–leukocyte interactions, complement amplification, NETosis, and immunothrombosis. Within the flavivirus group, DENV is used as the principal model for systemic vascular leakage, thrombocytopenia, and hemorrhagic risk; selected non-dengue flaviviruses illustrate how shared endothelial, platelet, and coagulation modules are redirected toward placental dysfunction (ZIKV), neuroinvasion (WNV and JEV), or hepatic failure and coagulopathy (YFV). Hantavirus infections provide a distinctive model of capillary leak syndrome in which non-lytic endothelial infection, immune-mediated injury, and permeability signaling converge on renal and pulmonary microvascular beds. A comparative view suggests that thrombotic, hemorrhagic, and leaky phenotypes are not mutually exclusive categories, but different outcomes of overlapping vascular programs shaped by viral tropism, vascular-bed specialization, immune activation, and host susceptibility.

title: Epidemiological Trends, Disease Burden, and Public Health Challenges in Nepal: A review
abstract: Natural disease severely impacts on human health to the least development countries like Nepal. The major challenge is epidemiological trend and diseases are burden in the public health. The communicable disease spreads soon and mass community become ill. Such event is harmful for country. The objective of this study is to analyse epidemiological trends, disease burden and public health challenges in Nepal. This is a review article. The research design is based on secondary data analysis and search topic related article form Google search and synthesis report cross sectional method. The published articles are related to communicable disease. The search articles synthesised and prepared cross sectional report. The articles were searched in 2018 to 2026. Practical academic implication of the study was epidemiological trend, communicable disease burden in public health challenges in Nepal. The communicable (infectious) disease found in Nepal are; waterborne illness (diarrhoea and dysentery, typhoid), vector borne infection (dengue, Malaria, kala-azar, scrub Typhus), respiratory disease (Tuberculosis (TB), and pneumonia, influenza). Communicable disease 'dengue' public health concern first time documented 2004 in Nepal. It effects started from Terai but now it is found in hills and mountain too. Health system of Nepal is delivering efficient preventive, curative and rehabilitative services.

title: Epidemiology of Chikungunya Virus Infection in the Philippines
abstract: Background: Chikungunya virus (CHIKV) has circulated in the Philippines for more than six decades. We systematically reviewed the epidemiology of CHIKV in the Philippines, integrating evidence on transmission, seroprevalence, diagnostics and molecular lineages. Methods: We searched PubMed and Embase to March 2026 for original studies reporting incidence, prevalence, seroprevalence, outbreak characteristics, or surveillance findings in human populations in the Philippines. The gray literature from the Department of Health (DOH) Epidemiology Bureau’s national chikungunya surveillance (2018–March 2026) was included separately. Findings were synthesized narratively because of substantial heterogeneity. Results: Sixteen studies and one national surveillance dataset were included. National surveillance recorded 12,662 cases from 2018 to early 2026, including 722 laboratory-confirmed cases and three fatalities. The Asian genotype predominated during the 2011–2013 epidemic, while Indian Ocean lineage (IOL) viruses were detected in southern Mindanao. Conclusions: Transmission of CHIKV in the Philippines is mostly sporadic with periods of low-level transmission. Because the clinical features overlap with dengue, acute febrile illness surveillance should test for both viruses.

title: Near or Far?
abstract: Dengue fever is a growing public health threat in urban Bangladesh, yet the role of hospital proximity as a spatial determinant of case detection remains largely untested. This chapter examines whether residents living closer to a dengue-treating hospital are more likely to be detected as cases, using cross-sectional survey data from two Dhaka sites: Dhaka Community Medical College Hospital (Boro Moghbazar) and Mugdha Medical College Hospital. Detection declined significantly with distance, and the effect persisted after adjustment for awareness, age, and prior infection, with each additional 100 meters of distance lowering the odds of detection by roughly 5%. Having an affected neighbor was the strongest correlate of detection, indicating fine-scale spatial clustering. Healthcare-worker responses revealed high knowledge but lower preventive practice, suggesting an institutional engagement gap. A divergent pattern in one distant zone coincided with localized drainage construction, suggesting environmental disturbances can temporarily override the proximity effect.
journal: Mitigation Measures for Environmental and Humanitarian Disasters

title: Genetic and immunological determinants of mosquito-borne virus susceptibility and climate change: Europe and Latin America-Caribbean perspectives
abstract: Climate change is rapidly altering the geographic distribution of mosquito-borne viruses (MBVs), increasing the risk of dengue, chikungunya, and Zika virus transmission in regions that have historically experienced limited exposure. While most studies have focused on environmental suitability and vector expansion, future disease patterns will also depend on host susceptibility and broader epidemiological and public health factors. In this Perspective, we discuss how climate-driven changes in exposure interact with host genetics, immune history, and public health preparedness to shape arboviral risk in Europe and Latin America and the Caribbean (LAC). We highlight how regional differences in immunogenetic diversity, HLA variation, and previous arboviral exposure influence susceptibility, disease severity, and vaccine responses, while accounting for substantial heterogeneity within both regions. Many European populations remain relatively immunologically naïve, whereas repeated arboviral exposure in parts of LAC has generated more complex immune landscapes shaped by previous infections, cross-reactivity, and immune imprinting. These differing exposure and susceptibility profiles have implications for surveillance, vaccination, and preparedness under a changing climate, although their contribution to population-level disease patterns requires further studies. Future risk assessments should therefore consider host susceptibility alongside climatic, ecological, epidemiological, and public health determinants. Integrating these factors could support more locally adapted prevention strategies and strengthen responses to both established arboviruses and emerging threats.

title: Analysis of Cell Populations from Arbovirus-Infected Tissues by Flow Cytometry.
abstract: Arboviruses still represent a major challenge to public health in many parts of the world. Despite shared epidemiological characteristics, each arboviral disorder displays distinct cellular tropism and activation patterns, progressing to immunopathological outcomes that remain not fully elucidated. A deeper understanding of these processes requires methodologies capable of characterizing the often-complex cellular responses. In this context, flow cytometry emerges as a valuable tool, enabling the characterization of heterogeneous cell populations, the assessment of activation and proliferation markers, the quantification of inflammatory mediators, and the detection of cell death pathways. By integrating these parameters, flow cytometry can enhance our understanding of arbovirus pathogenesis, clarify their cellular tropism, and understand immune responses to infection. This methodological article outlines the main steps for applying the technique to different target tissues infected by chikungunya, dengue, yellow fever, and Zika viruses, emphasizing the most effective strategies.

In this context, flow cytometry emerges as a valuable tool, enabling the characterization of heterogeneous cell populations, the assessment of activation and proliferation markers, the quantification of inflammatory mediators, and the detection of cell death pathways. By integrating these parameters, flow cytometry can enhance our understanding of arbovirus pathogenesis, clarify their cellular tropism, and understand immune responses to infection. This methodological article outlines the main steps for applying the technique to different target tissues infected by chikungunya, dengue, yellow fever, and Zika viruses, emphasizing the most effective strategies.

title: Development of a TaqMan-Based Multiplex Real-Time RTPCR Assay for Detection of Mosquito-Borne Viral Diseases
abstract: Background: Mosquito-borne viral diseases, including Dengue (DENV), Zika (ZIKV), Chikungunya (CHIKV), Yellow fever (YFV), and West Nile (WNV), represent a significant global health burden.Existing singleplex molecular assays are often time-consuming and resource-intensive.We aimed to develop and analytically validate a one-step multiplex TaqMan real-time RT-PCR assay for the simultaneous detection of these major arboviruses.Methods: Primers and hydrolysis probes were designed against conserved genomic regions.In vitro transcribed RNA standards were used to establish standard curves, determine PCR efficiency, and calculate limits of detection (LOD).A clinical validation panel comprising 250 samples with pre-determined infection statuses was used to assess diagnostic sensitivity and specificity against singleplex reference assays.Cross-reactivity was evaluated against a panel of related and unrelated pathogens. Results:The multiplex assay demonstrated linear detection across eight orders of magnitude (101 to 108 copies/μL) with PCR efficiencies ranging from 94.2% to 102.1% and coefficient of determination (R2) values ≥ 0.992 for all targets.The 95% LOD ranged from 10 to 50 copies/μL.No cross-reactivity was detected with any of the non-target organisms tested.In the clinical cohort, the assay achieved an overall diagnostic sensitivity of 98.0% (95% CI: 93.8-99.5%)and specificity of 100% (95% CI: 97.5-100%), with complete concordance observed between multiplex and singleplex assays for all targets except one low-titer ZIKV sample.Conclusion: The developed TaqMan multiplex qRT-PCR assay provides a rapid, sensitive, and highly specific platform for syndromic screening of major mosquito-borne viruses.The analytical and clinical validation framework supports its potential utility in both clinical diagnostics and vector surveillance programs.

title: VERTICAL TRANSMISSION OF ARBOVIRUSES: CLINICAL AND EPIDEMIOLOGICAL IMPLICATIONS IN BRAZIL
abstract: Arboviruses constitute an important public health problem in Brazil, especially due to the simultaneous circulation of different viruses and the potential for vertical transmission, with maternal, fetal, and neonatal repercussions. This study aims to analyze the clinical and epidemiological implications of vertical transmission of the main arboviruses in Brazil, with emphasis on Zika, Dengue, Chikungunya, and Oropouche viruses. For this purpose, a systematic literature review was conducted according to PRISMA recommendations, through searches in the SciELO, PubMed/MEDLINE, and LILACS databases, covering publications from 2015 to 2025. Evidence regarding transmission mechanisms, clinical manifestations, maternal-fetal outcomes, epidemiological aspects, and prevention and care strategies was analyzed. It was observed that Zika has a consolidated association with Congenital Zika Syndrome, whereas Dengue and Chikungunya have greater relevance of transmission near delivery. For Oropouche, recent evidence suggests potential placental and fetal infection, although further studies are needed. It is concluded that vertical transmission of arboviruses represents a relevant challenge to maternal and child health, reinforcing the need for epidemiological surveillance, early diagnosis, prenatal care, and prevention and care strategies.

title: Age-Dependent Distributions Of AedesTransmitted Infections
abstract: We propose a new approach to analyze the age-distribution of reported cases for vector-transmitted infections.Using officially reported cases of dengue, Zika, chikungunya, malaria and leishmaniasis for distinct geographical areas, in different periods.Data were treated in special but wellknown procedure, transforming the raw data into a density age-dependent distribution and fitting a special continuous function to it.We found that the proportion of age-dependent cases with respect to the total number of cases in a given year (or any transmission season) is probably determined by the ecological interactions between vectors and hosts.The age-distribution of the proportion of cases for the three Aedes-related infections are essentially the same independently of the magnitude of the outbreak and the geographical region considered.On the other hand, for the infections transmitted by other vectors, the age-distributions of the proportion of cases are entirely different.During specific outbreaks, the ratio between the age distribution of the proportion of officially reported cases and the total number of cases for Aedes transmitted infections such as dengue, chikungunya and zika is independent of the size of the outbreak, the size of the studied population, the period when the outbreak occurs; and the geographical region considered.Our results also suggest that the age-distribution of cases is mainly due to the interaction between vectors and their hosts.Since the interaction between the vectors and male and female hosts may be different, we investigate this and, in fact, the age-distribution is slightly different.

title: The impact of egg quiescence on the efficacy of Wolbachia-infected mosquito releases for arbovirus control
abstract: Abstract An ordinary differential model is proposed to understand the role of egg quiescence on the efficacy of releasing Wolbachia -infected mosquitoes to control arbovirus transmission. The model admits up to five equilibrium points and four biologically meaningful scenarios: extinction of both populations; persistence of the uninfected population with extinction of the infected one; persistence of the infected population with extinction of the uninfected one; and coexistence of both populations. This occurs because the coexistence scenario allows for bistability in the system. A sensitivity analysis shows that the effect of quiescence on mosquito fitness depends on the balance between survival and developmental progression under different environmental conditions. Because Wolbachia -infected eggs do not survive quiescence, or the adults that emerge are infertile, quiescence negatively impacts the fitness of infected mosquitoes, thereby reducing the prevalence of infection in the mosquito population. This increases the chance of encountering an uninfected mosquito, which is more likely to carry the dengue virus compared to a Wolbachia -infected one, potentially increasing the risk of dengue transmission during or after environmental stress that triggers quiescence. More importantly, quiescence can compromise the establishment of infection within the mosquito population by increasing the number of infected mosquitoes required during the release period. Therefore, the use of Wolbachia -infected mosquitoes to control arbovirus transmission in regions where quiescence occurs at a high rate can be jeopardized.

title: PERFIL EPIDEMIOLÓGICO, MICROBIOLÓGICO E IMUNOLÓGICO DAS INFECÇÕES CAUSADAS PELO VÍRUS OROPOUCHE - REVISÃO INTEGRATIVA
abstract: Introdução: A febre Oropouche é uma arbovirose causada pelo vírus zoonótico Oropouchevirus (OROV), membro da família Peribunyaviridae, que apresenta um genoma de RNA de fita simples segmentado, com alta capacidade de mutação. Os sintomas são semelhantes aos das arboviroses, como Dengue, Zika e Chikungunya, dessa forma, é crucial compreender as nuances específicas dessa patologia. O presente estudo objetiva apresentar as evidências científicas acerca do perfil epidemiológico, microbiológico e imunológico das infecções causadas pelo vírus Oropouche. Metodologia: Trata-se de uma revisão integrativa da literatura, cuja busca dos estudos foi realizada nas seguintes bases de dados: A Science Direct e National Library of Medicine National Institutes of Health (PubMed) foram analisados artigos publicados em 2020 a 2025, publicados em português e inglês. Utilizou-se o fluxograma do Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA). Resultados: Foram incluídos nessa revisão 11 artigos. O vírus tem se manifestado, predominantemente, na América do Sul e Central. Entre os estudos analisados 27,2% associaram diretamente glicoproteínas (Gn e Gc) à evasão da resposta imune e 36,4% descreveram alta variabilidade mutagênicas. Ao analisar as características imunológicas, notou-se 27,3% induz respostas imunes inata e adaptativa, mas há lacunas no entendimento da resposta humoral e celular de longa duração. Conclusão: É evidente que o OROV é emergente e responsável por uma infecção negligenciada, cuja expansão está relacionada à combinação de fatores ecológicos, microbiológicos, genéticos e imunológicos. Logo, estratégias que visam seu controle e mitigação devem incluir, por exemplo, abordagens de One Health. PALAVRAS-CHAVE: Infecções por Bunyaviridae; Epidemiologia; Microbiologia; Imunidade; Desenvolvimento de Vacinas.
authors: Luis Filipe Viana dos Santos Mota

title: Synergistic larvicidal effects of temephos and Bacillus thuringiensis israelensis against Aedes albopictus: a laboratory and field study
abstract: Background Aedes mosquito-borne diseases, such as dengue fever, pose significant challenges to global public health. Mosquito management is regarded as one of the most critical measures to control these diseases. Temephos has been widely used for larval mosquito control, but its sustained application has resulted in the emergence of resistance in many regions in China. Bacillus thuringiensis israelensis (Bti) offers an environmentally friendly alternative, but its field efficacy against late-instar larvae is limited. Previous studies have demonstrated the synergistic potential of combining temephos and Bti. Therefore, this study aims to determine the most effective combination ratio through laboratory bioassays and to evaluate the practical efficacy of this mixed formulation under field conditions. Methods Laboratory bioassays were conducted with early fourth-instar Aedes albopictus (Skuse, 1894) larvae to determine the co-toxicity coefficient (CTC) of 3 mixed formulations (temephos: Bti = 1:1, 1:3, and 1:5). In field trials, the mixed formulation with the greatest synergistic effect was used to evaluate its insecticidal effect under field conditions. A total of 150 natural breeding containers in one village in Shaoxing City were randomly selected and assigned to 3 groups (treatment group A, treatment group B, and the control group). Two application regimens (half-monthly application at twice the 99% lethal concentration [2 × LC99] vs. monthly application at 4 × LC99) were used in the treatment groups, and larval densities were monitored over a 3-month period to assess their larvicidal effects. Results The CTC values for all three mixed formulations were 141.477, 140.299, and 150.009, respectively (all exceeding 120), and mixed formulation C (temephos: Bti = 1:5) was selected for field trials. Over the 3-month period, the standard rates of reduction in mosquito larval density were 100.00%, 100.00%, and 100.00% in group A, while group B showed reductions of 96.80%, 87.03%, and 96.79%. Both treatment groups exhibited significantly lower larval densities than the control group ( p < 0.001), while no statistically significant difference was found between them. Conclusion The combination of temephos and Bti showed a synergistic effect under laboratory conditions, and the mixed formulation demonstrated effective larvicidal activity under field conditions.

Mosquito management is regarded as one of the most critical measures to control these diseases. Temephos has been widely used for larval mosquito control, but its sustained application has resulted in the emergence of resistance in many regions in China. Bacillus thuringiensis israelensis (Bti) offers an environmentally friendly alternative, but its field efficacy against late-instar larvae is limited. Previous studies have demonstrated the synergistic potential of combining temephos and Bti. Therefore, this study aims to determine the most effective combination ratio through laboratory bioassays and to evaluate the practical efficacy of this mixed formulation under field conditions. Methods Laboratory bioassays were conducted with early fourth-instar Aedes albopictus (Skuse, 1894) larvae to determine the co-toxicity coefficient (CTC) of 3 mixed formulations (temephos: Bti = 1:1, 1:3, and 1:5). In field trials, the mixed formulation with the greatest synergistic effect was used to evaluate its insecticidal effect under field conditions. A total of 150 natural breeding containers in one village in Shaoxing City were randomly selected and assigned to 3 groups (treatment group A, treatment group B, and the control group). Two application regimens (half-monthly application at twice the 99% lethal concentration [2 × LC99] vs. monthly application at 4 × LC99) were used in the treatment groups, and larval densities were monitored over a 3-month period to assess their larvicidal effects. Results The CTC values for all three mixed formulations were 141.477, 140.299, and 150.009, respectively (all exceeding 120), and mixed formulation C (temephos: Bti = 1:5) was selected for field trials. Over the 3-month period, the standard rates of reduction in mosquito larval density were 100.00%, 100.00%, and 100.00% in group A, while group B showed reductions of 96.80%, 87.03%, and 96.79%. Both treatment groups exhibited significantly lower larval densities than the control group ( p < 0.001), while no statistically significant difference was found between them. Conclusion The combination of temephos and Bti showed a synergistic effect under laboratory conditions, and the mixed formulation demonstrated effective larvicidal activity under field conditions.

title: Photonic crystal nanocavity refractive-index biosensor for multiple biological samples: A numerical study
abstract: Abstract This numerical study presents a two-dimensional photonic crystal (PhC) nanocavity biosensor based on a silicon slab for the refractive-index (RI) sensing of multiple biological samples, namely blood samples associated with tuberculosis, malaria, and dengue, and hemoglobin concentrations relevant to anemia assessment. The sensing performance is evaluated using the finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) method by analyzing the resonance wavelength shifts at the output port, while the photonic band structure is investigated using the plane-wave expansion (PWE) method. A 20 nm shift of the cavity-adjacent air hole provides the best overall sensor performance. Two-dimensional FDTD simulations based on the effective-index method yield an idealized sensitivity of 453.85 nm/RIU, a quality factor (QF) of 1.7348 × 105, a figure of merit (FOM) of 4.9740 × 104 RIU−1, and a detection limit (DL) of 2.01045 × 10−6 RIU for dengue-infected plasma. Full three-dimensional FDTD validation of the optimized design, which accounts for all radiative losses, gives a sensitivity of approximately 315 nm/RIU, a QF of 1.39 × 104, a FOM of 2.79 × 103 RIU−1, and a DL of 3.59 × 10−5 RIU for the same analyte. These results confirm the linear RI response of the sensor (R2 ≥ 0.9996), while showing that the 2D model overestimates the absolute QF by approximately one order of magnitude. The sensor also exhibits a linear and predictable thermal response of 98.8 pm/◦C over the range of 0–60 ◦C, which can be used for temperature calibration. A comparison with reported PhC sensors indicates that the proposed design is competitive. A fabrication-tolerance analysis shows that satisfactory sensing performance is maintained under random deviations in hole radius and position of up to 20 nm. With a compact footprint of 76.5 μm2 and compatibility with single-step lithography on a silicon-on-insulator platform, the proposed sensor is a promising candidate for label-free RI sensing in photonic integrated circuits. Surface functionalization and experimental validation will be required for disease-specific detection.

title: Educação, meio ambiente e saúde
abstract: As arboviroses Dengue, Zika e Chikungunya são transmitidas pelo mosquito Aedes aegypti e representam um grave problema de saúde pública, especialmente em regiões tropicais como o Brasil. O controle e a prevenção dessas doenças dependem de estratégias de aprendizagem, combate e divulgação, visando o engajamento social e a redução da proliferação do mosquito. Neste sentido o objetivo deste projeto concerne em desenvolver estratégias de aprendizagem, prevenção, combate e divulgação sobre as arboviroses Dengue, Zika e Chikungunya e sua relação com o descarte incorreto de resíduos na EEIEF Francisco André de Souza, Jucás, Ce. Trata-se de uma pesquisa de natureza aplicada com objetivos exploratórios e quanto aos procedimentos, uma pesquisa ação. As atividades desenvolvidas durante a execução do projeto foram bem-sucedidas, promovendo uma aprendizagem ativa e engajadora com os estudantes. As diversas estratégias didáticas, como jogos, maquetes e produção de vídeos educativos como podcasts e vídeos curtos, aprofundaram o conhecimento e incentivaram práticas sustentáveis e de cuidado com o meio ambiente e saúde. A iniciativa também extrapolou a escola, alcançando e conscientizando comunidades em Jucás e municípios vizinhos, demonstrando a eficácia das abordagens para enfrentar esse desafio.

title: A Comprehensive Review on Diverse aspects of Natural and Synthetic Mosquito Repellents
abstract: The present review was based on the diverse aspects of natural and synthetic mosquito repellents.Every year, 2.5 million cases of dengue & chikungunya are caused by the Aedes aegypti mosquito.Avoiding direct human-mosquito contact is the primary way to reduce mosquitoborne illnesses.It is highly advised that susceptible people who live in places where mosquitoes are still a possible threat apply insect repellents to all exposed skin areas.Warm-blooded animal's sweat contains lactic acid and CO2, which are attractive chemicals to mosquitoes.Essential oils, which are utilized as natural repellents, are mostly derived from plants.For instance, citronella oil, clove, eucalyptus, rosemary, peppermint, and lemon grass can deter mosquitoes.The most powerful synthetic repellent is N, N-diethyl-meta-toluamide (DEET), a toxic chemical that may produce carbon monoxide and a natural odor that resembles that of the human body.Moreover, 3-[N Butyl-N-acetyl]-amino propionic acid (IR3535) is the best mosquito repellent which is more effective than DEET for longer time.In conclusion, natural and synthetic mosquito repellents are effective in managing the insect's spread diseases.However, other methods including physical methods i.e., mosquito net, medicated net, non-medicated net, mosquito trap and mechanical methods i.e., electric zipper and mosquito's magnet are promising as strong mosquito repellent without any side effects to the host cell/body....
journal: International Journal of Drug Delivery Technology

title: Zika Virus–Associated Septic Shock in an Older Thai Patient: A Case Report and Literature Review
abstract: Zika virus (ZIKV) infection is generally a mild and self-limiting illness that most commonly presents with fever, rash, and arthralgia. Severe manifestations leading to significant morbidity or mortality are rare and generally occur in older adults with underlying comorbidities. Herein, we report the case of an 87-year-old man who presented with fever, confusion, hypotension, and dyspnea consistent with acute respiratory failure and septic shock. Chest radiography revealed pulmonary edema, while echocardiography revealed mildly impaired left ventricular systolic function. Increased cardiac biomarkers and a negative coronary angiogram suggested myocarditis. Molecular testing of the serum, cerebrospinal fluid, and endomyocardial tissue confirmed ZIKV infection. The patient was managed with intensive supportive care, including fluid resuscitation, vasopressors, and symptomatic treatment. His condition gradually improved following the resolution of septic shock and cardiac abnormalities. This case highlights the potential for severe ZIKV infection in older adults with comorbidities, underscoring the importance of considering ZIKV in the differential diagnosis of patients with fever, rashes, and septic shock in endemic regions. Early recognition and supportive management play critical roles in improving outcomes in severe ZIKV cases.
journal: Journal of Health Science and Medical Research

source_records.abstract: Zika virus (ZIKV) infection is generally a mild and self-limiting illness that most commonly presents with fever, rash, and arthralgia. Severe manifestations leading to significant morbidity or mortality are rare and generally occur in older adults with underlying comorbidities. Herein, we report the case of an 87-year-old man who presented with fever, confusion, hypotension, and dyspnea consistent with acute respiratory failure and septic shock. Chest radiography revealed pulmonary edema, while echocardiography revealed mildly impaired left ventricular systolic function. Increased cardiac biomarkers and a negative coronary angiogram suggested myocarditis. Molecular testing of the serum, cerebrospinal fluid, and endomyocardial tissue confirmed ZIKV infection. His condition gradually improved following the resolution of septic shock and cardiac abnormalities. This case highlights the potential for severe ZIKV infection in older adults with comorbidities, underscoring the importance of considering ZIKV in the differential diagnosis of patients with fever, rashes, and septic shock in endemic regions. Early recognition and supportive management play critical roles in improving outcomes in severe ZIKV cases.

title: Structure-Guided Optimization of a LipL32-Targeting DNA Aptamer through Molecular Dynamics and Free-Energy Analysis
abstract: Abstract Accurate detection of leptospirosis requires high-affinity recognition of the conserved LipL32 biomarker. Although LipL32-targeting DNA aptamers have been identified through systematic evolution of ligands by exponential enrichment (SELEX), the molecular basis of their target recognition remains unclear, limiting rational post-SELEX optimization. Here, we investigated the molecular recognition mechanism of the LepDapt-5 aptamer family using molecular dynamics (MD) simulations and binding free-energy analysis. We generated three-dimensional aptamer models using AlphaFold 3 (AF3) and constructed protein–aptamer docking complexes with HADDOCK, showing a stable G-quadruplex (GQ) motif within the aptamer core. Structural and energetic analyses identified key domains contributing to LipL32 binding, while per-residue energy decomposition highlighted nucleotides suitable for rational sequence refinement. Guided by these insights, we introduced targeted single-point mutations, evaluated their effects computationally, and validated their performance experimentally using enzyme-linked aptamer sorbent assays (ELASA). Relative binding free energies (ΔΔGbind) calculated using nonequilibrium alchemical MD showed strong agreement with ELASA measurements: T19A reduced binding affinity, G7C produced minimal change, and G24C significantly enhanced affinity. Experimental equilibrium dissociation constants (KD) further supported these predictions, identifying G24C as the highest-affinity variant. Additionally, the G24C mutant retained strong binding to LipL32 while exhibiting no detectable binding to the NS1 protein of dengue virus 2 and the E2 protein of Chikungunya virus.

title: Molecular Detection of Arboviruses in Aedes spp. Larvae During Entomo-Virological Surveillance in a Hospital Area of Brasília, Federal District, Brazil
abstract: ABSTRACT Background: Arboviruses in hospital environments may represent a neglected risk of nosocomial infections. This study investigated arboviruses in Aedes spp. larvae collected from a hospital area in Brasília, Federal District, Brazil. Methods: Eighteen ovitraps were deployed for 26 weeks. larvae were pooled weekly, and viral detection was performed by reverse transcription-quantitative PCR. Results: Dengue virus serotypes 1, 2, and 4, Zika virus, and Chikungunya virus were identified, with an overall positivity rate of 30.76%. Conclusion: The surveillance strategy effectively detected arboviral RNA in a hospital setting, suggesting local arboviral circulation associated with the transmission triad.
authors: Mércia Tayane Pereira dos Santos de Oliveira
journal: Revista da Sociedade Brasileira de Medicina Tropical

title: COINFECTION WITH PLASMODIUM VIVAX AND CHIKUNGUNYA; WHEN FEBRILE ILLNESS EVOLVES INTO HYPERDYNAMIC SHOCK: CASE REPORT
abstract: Coinfection with malaria and chikungunya is a rare presentation and poses a diagnostic challenge., especially since both infections can produce systemic manifestations and hemodynamic compromise. We present the case of a 23-year-old female patient from an urban area with no known past medical history, who presented with a seven-day history of fever, dizziness, generalized weakness, arthralgia, and vomiting. On admission, she was febrile, tachycardic, and hypotensive, with an insufficient hemodynamic response to initial resuscitation with crystalloids, requiring vasopressor support. Advanced cardiovascular evaluation revealed a predominantly vasodilatory and hyperdynamic profile, characterized by high cardiac output, decreased systemic vascular resistance, and preserved stroke volume. Left and right ventricular systolic and diastolic function remained preserved, with adequate TAPSE and MAPSE, and no significant chamber dilation or regional contractility abnormalities. The electrocardiogram and cardiac enzymes showed no evidence of myocardial injury or myocarditis. Studies revealed severe anemia, with a hemoglobin level of 6 g/ dL, and hepatosplenomegaly. Thick blood smear identified Plasmodium. The patient tested positive for vivax, while the PCR test for chikungunya was positive and the dengue test was negative, confirming the coinfection. Intravenous artesunate was initiated, followed by artemether-lumefantrine, in addition to vasoactive support and transfusion of two units of packed red blood cells. The patient experienced progressive hemodynamic recovery and a favorable clinical course. This case highlights the importance of considering vector-borne coinfections and characterizing the hemodynamic phenotype to differentiate vasodilatory shock from cardiogenic compromise.
journal: World Journal of Advanced Research and Reviews

title: Efectos del cambio climático en la distribución de enfermedades vectoriales en Latinoamérica: revisión sistemática
abstract: Objetivo: analizar los efectos del cambio climático en la distribución de las enfermedades transmitidas por vectores en Latinoamérica y su impacto en la población. Método: revisión sistemática con síntesis narrativa en PubMed y SciELO (2012-2025); se incluyeron 15 estudios: seis de modelización, cuatro ecológicos o de series temporales y cinco revisiones. Resultados: los modelos proyectan la expansión de Aedes aegypti hacia nuevas latitudes y altitudes. Las anomalías térmicas, las olas de calor y la variación estacional se asociaron con la transmisión del dengue y otras arbovirosis. La deforestación amazónica impulsa la malaria, y el clima modifica la distribución de los triatominos. Conclusión: el cambio climático amplía el riesgo vectorial y exige vigilancia integrada.

title: Arboviroses no município de Limoeiro: análise dos registros entre 2021 e 2025 e ação educativa no ensino médio
abstract: As arboviroses constituem um importante problema de saúde pública e sua abordagem no ambiente escolar pode contribuir para a compreensão das formas de transmissão e prevenção. Este estudo teve como objetivo analisar os registros de dengue, chikungunya e zika no município de Limoeiro, Pernambuco, entre 2021 e 2025, e descrever uma ação educativa realizada com estudantes do ensino médio. Desenvolveu-se um estudo descritivo, de abordagem quantitativa, organizado em duas etapas complementares. Na primeira, foram analisados dados secundários fornecidos pela Secretaria Municipal de Saúde de Limoeiro e consultados no DATASUS, mediante o cálculo de frequências absolutas e relativas. Na segunda, realizou-se uma intervenção com uma turma do 1o ano da Escola de Referência em Ensino Médio Dr. Sebastião de Vasconcelos Galvão, composta por uma palestra dialogada e pelo jogo ‘Bingo temático: arboviroses’. No período analisado, foram contabilizados 4.784 registros: 4.203 de dengue (87,9%), 471 de chikungunya (9,8%) e 110 de zika (2,3%). A dengue predominou em todos os anos e alcançou 1.621 registros em 2025. Durante a ação educativa, observaram-se participação, interação e cooperação entre os estudantes. Conclui-se que a utilização de informações epidemiológicas locais, associada a uma atividade lúdica, pode aproximar os conteúdos científicos da realidade escolar e favorecer o diálogo sobre prevenção. Entretanto, a ausência de avaliação sistemática limita as conclusões sobre os efeitos da intervenção na aprendizagem.
authors: Rita de Cássia Freire de Melo Goldbaum
journal: Revista edUCA - Revista Multidisciplinar da Faculdade Católica Paulista

Este estudo teve como objetivo analisar os registros de dengue, chikungunya e zika no município de Limoeiro, Pernambuco, entre 2021 e 2025, e descrever uma ação educativa realizada com estudantes do ensino médio. Desenvolveu-se um estudo descritivo, de abordagem quantitativa, organizado em duas etapas complementares. Na primeira, foram analisados dados secundários fornecidos pela Secretaria Municipal de Saúde de Limoeiro e consultados no DATASUS, mediante o cálculo de frequências absolutas e relativas. Na segunda, realizou-se uma intervenção com uma turma do 1o ano da Escola de Referência em Ensino Médio Dr. Sebastião de Vasconcelos Galvão, composta por uma palestra dialogada e pelo jogo ‘Bingo temático: arboviroses’. No período analisado, foram contabilizados 4.784 registros: 4.203 de dengue (87,9%), 471 de chikungunya (9,8%) e 110 de zika (2,3%). A dengue predominou em todos os anos e alcançou 1.621 registros em 2025. Durante a ação educativa, observaram-se participação, interação e cooperação entre os estudantes. Conclui-se que a utilização de informações epidemiológicas locais, associada a uma atividade lúdica, pode aproximar os conteúdos científicos da realidade escolar e favorecer o diálogo sobre prevenção. Entretanto, a ausência de avaliação sistemática limita as conclusões sobre os efeitos da intervenção na aprendizagem.

title: Whose sepsis? Tropical infections and the limits of contemporary sepsis evidence
abstract: Dear Editor, Sepsis is among the leading causes of death worldwide. Before the COVID-19 pandemic, the Global Burden of Disease Study estimated 48.9 million incident cases and 11.0 million sepsis-related deaths in 2017, almost one in five deaths globally.1 Over recent decades, randomized controlled trials have substantially refined the management of sepsis and critical illness. Lung-protective ventilation, safer haemodynamic strategies, appropriate vasopressor use, and evidence-based supportive care now underpin contemporary practice and represent some of the most important achievements of modern critical care. Yet a paradox persists. The greatest burden of sepsis falls on sub-Saharan Africa, South and Southeast Asia, and Oceania,1 precisely the regions where dengue, malaria, leptospirosis, scrub typhus, melioidosis, and other tropical infections drive a substantial share of severe illness and critical-care admission. Despite this, the representation of these infections in landmark sepsis and acute respiratory distress syndrome trials is difficult to determine. Causative pathogens are frequently absent, grouped into broad microbiological categories, or not reported separately, making it unclear whether individual tropical infections were excluded, underrepresented, or simply not identifiable (Table S1). The practical consequence is the same. Clinicians must extrapolate evidence largely generated in sepsis populations dominated by pneumonia, intra-abdominal infection, urinary infection, and healthcare-associated infection to pathogen-defined syndromes with potentially different pathophysiology.
journal: Transactions of the Royal Society of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene

title: EFFECTIVENESS OF HOMOEOPATHIC MEDICINE RHUS TOXICODENDRON IN THE MANAGEMENT OF POST-FEVER ARTHRALGIA: A PROSPECTIVE OBSERVATIONAL STUDY
abstract: BackgroundPost-fever arthralgia is a frequently encountered clinical condition that persists after the resolution of acute febrile illnesses, particularly viral infections such as chikungunya, dengue, influenza, and other viral fevers.Although the acute infection subsides, many patients continue to experience persistent joint pain, stiffness, reduced mobility, and impaired quality of life for several weeks or even months.Conventional management mainly consists of analgesics, NSAIDs, physiotherapy, and supportive measures.Homoeopathy adopts an individualized therapeutic approach.Rhus toxicodendron is commonly indicated for musculoskeletal disorders characterized by stiffness and pain relieved by continued motion.This study evaluated its effectiveness in post-fever arthralgia.Objective To evaluate the effectiveness of homoeopathic medicine Rhus toxicodendron in the management of post-fever arthralgia using the Numeric Pain Rating Scale (NPRS) and WHOQOL-BREF questionnaire.Methods A prospective observational study was conducted among 40 patients diagnosed with post-fever arthralgia.Eligible patients aged 18-60 years were enrolled after informed consent.Individualized homoeopathic treatment with Rhus toxicodendron where indicated was prescribed.Patients were followed weekly for four weeks.Outcomes were assessed using NPRS and WHOQOL-BREF.Statistical analysis was performed using paired t-test. ResultsA total of 40 participants completed the 4-week study (mean age: 36.9 ± 10.8 years; 55% female).Chikungunya was the most common preceding febrile illness (40%), followed by viral fever (27.5%), dengue (25%), and malaria (7.5%).The mean Numeric Pain Rating Scale (NPRS) score significantly decreased from 7.3 ± 1.1 at baseline to 2.2 ± 1.0 after treatment (mean difference: 5.1; p < 0.001).Significant improvements were also observed in all WHOQOL-BREF domains, including physical, psychological, social, and environmental health (p < 0.001 for all).No serious adverse events were reported, and all participants completed follow-up.Conclusion Individualized homoeopathic treatment with Rhus toxicodendron, where indicated, may contribute to symptomatic improvement in post-fever arthralgia.Larger randomized controlled trials are warranted.
journal: International Journal of Drug Delivery Technology

title: Synthese van gefuseerde isothiazole derivaten als inhibitoren van het ‘cyclin G-associated kinase’ (GAK)
abstract: Previous research in our lab led to the discovery of 6-aryl-isothiazolo[4,3-b]pyridines as potent and selective inhibitors of either cyclin G associated kinase (GAK). This kinase is a promising drug target for the development of broadspectrum antiviral agents. Using the current chemistry, 3,6-disubstituted isothiazolo[4,3-b]pyridines can easily be prepared. In this project proposal, we will focus on the establishment of synthetic procedures to have access to novel fused isothiazolo derivatives, which will allow us to broaden chemical space that can be studied as GAK inhibitors. The design will be guided by molecular modeling and biochemical kinase assays. Promising compounds will be investigated for activity against various viruses, such as the dengue virus and the venezuelan equine encephalitis virus.

title: Factors Associated with Divergent Introgression Outcomes from Wolbachia-Based Interventions in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil
abstract: Wolbachia-based interventions were less effective in achieving introgression in Rio de Janeiro than other settings. Reduced introgression occurred in locations where dengue was historically high, raising concerns of inequity. We examined factors affecting Wolbachia introgression in Rio through trajectory modeling, spatiotemporal Bayesian models, and Ae. aegypti abundance estimation. During the intervention (2017-2020), Wolbachia introgression was 26% (median; IQR,14-44%), with four distinct trajectories. Despite receiving more releases, densely populated areas with low socioeconomic status had lower introgression. In spatiotemporally explicit multivariable regressions, higher Ae. aegypti abundance, temperature, population density and lower socioeconomic status were associated with reduced introgression. Improved characterization of Ae. aegypti abundance and other structural/environmental predictors of introgression could be used to calibrate release doses to ensure equitable benefits from Wolbachia interventions.

full_text: AbstractVector-borne diseases (VBD) caused by arboviruses represent a major public health threat in tropical regions. According to WHO’s Global Vector Control Response, more than 80% of the global population live in areas at risk for VBD. For instance, Aedes aegypti is the primary vector of dengue virus (DENV) and chikungunya virus (CHIKV), and its widespread distribution, particularly in Brazil, contributes to the occurrence of outbreaks. During these outbreaks, mosquitoes may acquire either monoinfections or coinfections, which can occur either simultaneously or sequentially, potentially influencing transmission dynamics. In this study, we investigated the effects of simultaneous coinfection with CHIKV and two DENV serotypes (DENV-1 and DENV-2) on the vector competence of Ae. aegypti and described the characteristics of infection and transmission phenotypes following different orders of sequential arbovirus acquisition. Simultaneous coinfection resulted in serotype-dependent outcomes. At 7 days post-infection (dpi), DENV-1 infection rates and viral loads were significantly reduced compared with monoinfections, whereas DENV-2 showed increased viral loads in saliva. At 14 dpi, CHIKV infection rates were significantly reduced in both the CHIKV+DENV-1 (CD1) and CHIKV+DENV-2 (CD2) groups, whereas CHIKV viral loads were reduced only in the CD2 group. In the sequential coinfection experiments, DENV-2 exhibited lower replication levels than DENV-1 in both sequential infection scenarios, regardless of whether DENV was acquired before or after CHIKV. Likewise, DENV-2 showed lower transmission efficiency than DENV-1, and murine transmission assays confirmed reduced viral loads for DENV-2. Overall, our findings demonstrate that CHIKV–DENV coinfection in Ae. aegypti is associated with distinct infection and transmission outcomes depending on the DENV serotype and the infection scenario. In sequentially exposed mosquitoes, distinct phenotypes were observed according to the order of arbovirus acquisition. These results highlight the complexity of arboviral coinfections within this shared vector and emphasize the importance of considering different coinfection scenarios when evaluating vector competence and transmission risk in endemic settings.Keywords: Aedes aegypti, arbovirus coinfection, chikungunya virus, dengue virus serotypes, sequential infection, simultaneous infection, vector competence 2.Materials and methods2.1. Ae. aegypti colony A well-established Brazilian colony of Ae. aegypti (strain BH), maintained at the Laboratory of Medical Entomology, Fiocruz-Minas, Brazil, was used in this study. full_text_sections.abstract: AbstractVector-borne diseases (VBD) caused by arboviruses represent a major public health threat in tropical regions. According to WHO’s Global Vector Control Response, more than 80% of the global population live in areas at risk for VBD. For instance, Aedes aegypti is the primary vector of dengue virus (DENV) and chikungunya virus (CHIKV), and its widespread distribution, particularly in Brazil, contributes to the occurrence of outbreaks. During these outbreaks, mosquitoes may acquire either monoinfections or coinfections, which can occur either simultaneously or sequentially, potentially influencing transmission dynamics. In this study, we investigated the effects of simultaneous coinfection with CHIKV and two DENV serotypes (DENV-1 and DENV-2) on the vector competence of Ae. aegypti and described the characteristics of infection and transmission phenotypes following different orders of sequential arbovirus acquisition. Simultaneous coinfection resulted in serotype-dependent outcomes. At 7 days post-infection (dpi), DENV-1 infection rates and viral loads were significantly reduced compared with monoinfections, whereas DENV-2 showed increased viral loads in saliva. At 14 dpi, CHIKV infection rates were significantly reduced in both the CHIKV+DENV-1 (CD1) and CHIKV+DENV-2 (CD2) groups, whereas CHIKV viral loads were reduced only in the CD2 group. In the sequential coinfection experiments, DENV-2 exhibited lower replication levels than DENV-1 in both sequential infection scenarios, regardless of whether DENV was acquired before or after CHIKV. Likewise, DENV-2 showed lower transmission efficiency than DENV-1, and murine transmission assays confirmed reduced viral loads for DENV-2. Overall, our findings demonstrate that CHIKV–DENV coinfection in Ae. aegypti is associated with distinct infection and transmission outcomes depending on the DENV serotype and the infection scenario. In sequentially exposed mosquitoes, distinct phenotypes were observed according to the order of arbovirus acquisition. These results highlight the complexity of arboviral coinfections within this shared vector and emphasize the importance of considering different coinfection scenarios when evaluating vector competence and transmission risk in endemic settings.Keywords: Aedes aegypti, arbovirus coinfection, chikungunya virus, dengue virus serotypes, sequential infection, simultaneous infection, vector competence

full_text_sections.discussion: 4.DiscussionThis study examines the transmission dynamics associated with two ecologically relevant coinfection scenarios, namely, simultaneous and sequential coinfection, using two epidemiologically significant arboviruses: dengue virus (DENV) and chikungunya virus (CHIKV). Under monoinfection conditions in vitro, DENV-2 has consistently demonstrated elevated viral replication levels relative to DENV-3 (Quintero-Gil et al., 2014; Niu et al., 2020) and DENV-1 (Quintero-Gil et al., 2018). Complementary in vivo studies employing Ae. aegypti and Aedes albopictus infected with the four DENV serotypes have similarly reported enhanced viral loads for DENV-1 and DENV-2 when compared with DENV-3 and DENV-4 (Ekwudu et al., 2020). These serotype-specific differences in viral replication kinetics may contribute to differences in vector competence, transmission efficiency, and overall epidemiological potential and should therefore be considered when interpreting coinfection experiments involving different DENV serotypes.These serotype-specific differences in viral replication kinetics may significantly modulate vector competence, transmission efficiency, and overall epidemiological potential, particularly in contexts of coinfection with CHIKV.Under coinfection conditions, the structural and functional distinctions between the genera Alphavirus and Orthoflavivirus may contribute to different outcomes in the infection and transmission processes of Ae. aegypti. Although both viruses share the same vector and are positive-sense single-stranded RNA viruses, they differ in structural features, replication strategies, and interactions with the mosquito immune system. Alphaviruses replicate in the cytoplasm (Laurent et al., 2022; Girard et al., 2024), whereas orthoflaviviruses preferentially establish replication complexes associated with the rough endoplasmic reticulum (RER) (Welsch et al., 2009; Rückert and Ebel, 2018). These biological disparities may influence coinfection dynamics and could partially elucidate the antagonistic or synergistic interactions identified in our study.In simultaneous coinfection, CHIKV was associated with reductions in both the prevalence and viral load of DENV-1 at 7 dpi. These results suggest that CHIKV was associated with reduced DENV-1 replication when Ae. aegypti mosquitoes were co-infected with both viral species. However, this effect did not extend to viral loads in saliva or transmission efficiency, indicating that horizontal transmission to vertebrate hosts was not significantly affected. A potential area for further investigation is the impact of this interaction on vertical transmission of DENV-1, since reduced viral load and prevalence in the mosquito body may limit successful viral passage to progeny during the early post-infection period.This finding is consistent with studies that demonstrate a similar effect in interactions between CHIKV and ZIKV (Rückert et al., 2017) and between MAYV and ZIKV (Brustolin et al., 2023), in which ZIKV viral load was reduced. Differences in coinfection outcomes are also reflected in vitro. In C6/36 cells, when DENV-3 was introduced at a higher multiplicity of infection (MOI = 1.0) than CHIKV (MOI = 0.1), only DENV replication was detected, indicating inhibition of CHIKV replication (Potiwat et al., 2011). Conversely, in Vero and human liver cells, CHIKV replication increased while DENV replication decreased (Zaidi et al., 2018; Taraphdar et al., 2022). These findings emphasize that coinfection dynamics are context-dependent, with outcomes varying by host, cell type, and virus strain. Notably, in mosquitoes, CHIKV viral load also increased during simultaneous coinfection with orthoflaviviruses (Rodrigues et al., 2021).In contrast to DENV-1, simultaneous CHIKV coinfection did not increase whole-body DENV-2 viral loads but was associated with significantly higher viral loads in saliva. This finding suggests that CHIKV may facilitate DENV-2 dissemination to, or release from, the salivary glands without necessarily increasing systemic viral loads. However, this interpretation should be considered with caution because viral loads were quantified using whole mosquito homogenates rather than dissected salivary glands. Consequently, the present study cannot determine whether the increased salivary viral load resulted from enhanced dissemination to the salivary glands or from greater viral accumulation within this tissue. Nevertheless, elevated salivary viral loads remain epidemiologically relevant because a higher viral inoculum delivered during mosquito feeding is more likely to establish productive infections in vertebrate hosts by increasing the probability of overcoming early innate immune responses (Althouse et al., 2014; Le Coupanec et al., 2017).An additional observation was the marked reduction in DENV-2 detection at 21 dpi in both the monoinfection and simultaneous coinfection groups. Because independent groups of mosquitoes were analyzed at each sampling time point, this pattern should not be interpreted as evidence of viral clearance within individual mosquitoes. Rather, it indicates that a smaller proportion of mosquitoes had detectable DENV-2 infection at 21 dpi.At 14 dpi, DENV-1 coinfection was associated with reduced CHIKV prevalence, while DENV-2 coinfection was associated with reductions in both CHIKV prevalence and viral load. These results suggest that both dengue serotypes may negatively influence CHIKV replication and/or establishment during later infection stages. A decrease in prevalence may translate into reduced vertical transmission potential of CHIKV, given that fewer females remain infected and capable of transmitting virus to progeny. In the case of DENV-2, the reduction in CHIKV viral load further strengthens this hypothesis, as lower systemic loads may reduce the likelihood of viral dissemination to the ovaries and subsequent establishment of transovarial infection (Ciota and Kramer, 2010; Vazeille et al., 2010). However, transmission efficiency and CHIKV salivary load remained unaffected, suggesting that coinfection may not substantially alter horizontal transmission from mosquitoes to vertebrate hosts.An important consideration is that CHIKV transmission to vertebrate hosts may occur considerably earlier than 14 dpi. Previous studies have demonstrated the rapid progression of CHIKV through mosquito tissue barriers and its relatively short extrinsic incubation period, with infectious virus being detected in saliva during the first days after exposure. Moreover, arbovirus infection and transmission are dynamic processes, and salivary gland infection or viral release into saliva may vary substantially over time (Robison et al., 2020; Viginier et al., 2023; Sartsanga et al., 2025). Therefore, because transmission was assessed at a single, relatively late time point in the present study, transient differences in CHIKV transmission between monoinfected and coinfected mosquitoes may not have been detected. Our findings should thus be interpreted as showing no detectable effect on CHIKV transmission at 14 dpi, rather than demonstrating the absence of an effect throughout the extrinsic incubation period. Since both DENV-1 and DENV-2 were associated with reduced CHIKV infection outcomes, biological features shared across dengue serotypes, such as overlapping cell tropism or conserved patterns of immune stimulation, may represent potential explanations that warrant further investigation. Potential mechanisms underlying these viral interactions include: (i) competition for target cells in the midgut or secondary tissues; (ii) competition for cellular and metabolic resources, including the host translational machinery and energy pools; and (iii) modulation of mosquito immune responses, because arboviruses may differentially activate RNA interference pathways, Toll/IMD signaling, or other innate responses, thereby affecting the replication and dissemination of the secondary virus…
full_text_sections.conclusion: 5.ConclusionOur findings demonstrate that simultaneous CHIKV and DENV coinfection and different orders of sequential arbovirus exposure are associated with distinct infection and transmission phenotypes in Ae. aegypti. These observations highlight the complexity of arbovirus coinfections within mosquito vectors and indicate that their outcomes may vary according to the DENV serotype and infection scenario.During simultaneous coinfection, DENV-1 showed greater reductions in systemic infection and viral replication than DENV-2, while the sequential exposure experiments revealed distinct infection and transmission phenotypes between groups involving DENV-1- and DENV-2 and across different orders of virus acquisition. Although differences in salivary viral loads were observed under specific conditions, transmission efficiency was evaluated only at a single, relatively late time point (14 dpi). Therefore, the present study cannot exclude the possibility that coinfection may affect earlier stages of viral dissemination to saliva or the duration of the extrinsic incubation period.The sequential infection experiments should, however, be interpreted within the limitations of the experimental design. Matched sequential controls in which mosquitoes received a non-infectious blood meal followed by DENV-1 or DENV-2 seven days later were not included. Consequently, the specific effect of prior CHIKV infection on each DENV serotype cannot be distinguished from other effects associated with sequential exposure. In addition, differences observed between DENV-1 and DENV-2 may reflect intrinsic differences in their vector competence and replication dynamics and should therefore not be interpreted as evidence of a differential CHIKV-mediated effect on the two serotypes.Additional limitations should also be considered. The use of a single Ae. aegypti population and one viral strain per arbovirus limits the generalizability of the findings, and the cellular and molecular mechanisms underlying the observed patterns were not directly investigated. Thus, it remains unclear to what extent intracellular competition, mosquito immune responses, tissue tropism, or other processes contribute to the observed coinfection phenotypes.Taken together, our findings characterize distinct infection and transmission phenotypes associated with simultaneous coinfection and different sequential arbovirus exposure scenarios under laboratory conditions. Future studies incorporating matched sequential controls, multiple mosquito populations and viral genotypes, additional transmission time points, and mechanistic approaches will be important to determine the specific contribution of virus–virus interactions to these phenotypes and establish whether the observed patterns extend to natural transmission settings where DENV and CHIKV cocirculate.
full_text_sections.other: 1.IntroductionVector-borne diseases (VBDs) are caused by parasites, viruses, and bacteria and are transmitted to humans and other vertebrates through the bite of infected blood-sucking arthropods, such as mosquitoes, ticks, and sandflies. Of the 1, 407 recognized species of human pathogens, 177 are classified as emerging or re-emerging, with approximately 73% of these being arboviruses transmitted by mosquitoes (Mbaoma et al., 2025). It is estimated that nearly 80% of the world’s population lives in areas at risk of exposure to at least one VBD, which collectively are responsible for more than 700, 000 deaths annually (Madewell, 2020; Manouana et al., 2024; World Health Organization, 2024a).Dengue virus (DENV) and Chikungunya virus (CHIKV) are primarily transmitted by mosquitoes of the genus Aedes, particularly Aedes aegypti the principal urban vector in tropical and subtropical regions worldwide. However, Aedes albopictus has emerged as an important secondary vector, contributing to the maintenance and geographic expansion of both arboviruses, particularly in temperate regions and areas where Ae. aegypti is absent or less abundant (Bezerra et al., 2016; Resck et al., 2024). Among the 134 arboviruses known to cause disease in humans, DENV and CHIKV are among the most prevalent and clinically important (Gubler, 2001). DENV and CHIKV belong to the genera Orthoflavivirus (formerly Flavivirus) and Alphavirus, respectively (Postler et al., 2023).Historical accounts indicate that China first documented dengue as a disease as early as 265–420 CE. More reliable records of epidemics in North America, Asia, and Africa emerged between 1779 and 1780. The growth of international trade and transportation in the 19th century facilitated the global spread of dengue, particularly through port towns, and its incidence continued to increase during the 20th century. In contrast, chikungunya was first recognized during an outbreak in Tanzania in 1952, when CHIKV was subsequently isolated and identified. Today, both diseases are widespread worldwide (Lumsden, 1955; World Health Organization, 2024b).While outbreaks of diseases with clinical manifestations compatible with dengue have been reported for centuries, the first isolations of DENV-1 and DENV-2 serotypes occurred in 1943 in Japan and 1945 in Hawaii, respectively (Hotta, 1952)., DENV is currently classified into four serotypes (DENV-1 to DENV-4), which share approximately 65% ​​genomic sequence identity and are endemic in more than 100 countries (Messina et al., 2014; Sirisena et al., 2021). CHIKV was first isolated for the first time in 1952 in Tanzania, Africa, and has since spread worldwide (Lumsden, 1955; World Health Organization, 2024b). In Brazil, the circulation of DENV has been documented since the 1980s, with outbreaks recurring every two to five years (Brathwaite Dick et al., 2012; Salles et al., 2018). CHIKV was introduced into Brazil in 2014, resulting in regional outbreaks, particularly in the southeast of the country (Almeida et al., 2023).Aedes aegypti, the primary vector of DENV and CHIKV, is currently widespread throughout Brazil; a distribution driven by poor urban infrastructure, population growth, and socioeconomic inequality (Torres et al., 2024). Additionally, factors such as increased urban mobility, climate and environmental changes, and the lack of effective vector control policies have contributed to the expansion of this vector and, consequently, to the increasing incidence of arboviral diseases (Ministério da Saúde, 2025). According to official surveillance data from Brazil, there were approximately 6 million dengue cases in 2024, compared with approximately 1.5 million cases in 2025. Similarly, approximately 230, 000 chikungunya cases were reported in 2024, decreasing to approximately 100, 000 cases in 2025 (Ministério da Saúde, 2024, 2025).The coexistence of multiple arboviruses in endemic areas raises concerns about coinfections in both humans and vectors. Although CHIKV-affected areas often overlap with regions endemic for DENV (Mackenzie et al., 2001), the rarity of simultaneous outbreaks raises the question of whether such events are truly uncommon or simply underreported. Nevertheless, confirmed cases of DENV and CHIKV coinfection in humans have been reported in Brazil (Torres et al., 2024), Madagascar (Ratsitorahina et al., 2008), Gabon, Central Africa (Caron et al., 2012), the Caribbean (Omarjee et al., 2014) and the Colombia–Venezuela border region (Carrillo-Hernández et al., 2018).Coinfection can occur by two mechanisms: (i) simultaneous infection with multiple viruses through a single mosquito bite, or (ii) sequential infection, in which the host receives infective bites from mosquitoes infected with different arboviruses (Miralles et al., 2001; Chaves et al., 2018). Studies have reported that Ae. aegypti can simultaneously transmit Zika virus (ZIKV) and CHIKV through its saliva, with transmission rates as high as 12% for both viruses (Göertz et al., 2017). In Brazil, Ae. aegypti populations from Manaus are highly permissive to DENV/ZIKV coinfections and can transmit both pathogens during a single bite, with increased transmission efficiency observed for ZIKV to vertebrate hosts (Chaves et al., 2018). Furthermore, the dynamics of dual or triple coinfections can alter vector competence and the viral abundance of one or more viruses (Rodrigues et al., 2021). Evidence for the occurrence of coinfections in nature is provided by reports of vertical transmission from female mosquitoes to their offspring, resulting in larvae simultaneously infected with DENV and ZIKV (Teixeira et al., 2021).Sequential coinfections, in which a mosquito already infected with one arbovirus is later exposed to another, are considered more likely to occur than simultaneous coinfections. Importantly, the interactions between the vector and each virus under these conditions can differ substantially, sometimes leading to unexpected effects on vector competence (Peng et al., 2024). Primary arbovirus infections can modulate vector susceptibility to subsequent infections by influencing viral replication, dissemination, and transmission efficiency. Consequently, these interactions may alter viral abundance and vector competence, thereby influencing the circulation of co-circulating arboviruses and the dynamics of outbreaks in endemic regions (Rodrigues et al., 2021). In the case of DENV and ZIKV, an initial DENV infection has been shown to reduce ZIKV dissemination in C6/36 cells and in Ae. aegypti (Rückert et al., 2017; Peng et al., 2024). Conversely, synergistic interactions have also been reported. Ae. aegypti infected with CHIKV either before or after exposure to ZIKV exhibited increased ZIKV transmission at seven days after the second infection (Magalhaes et al., 2018). Similarly, prior ZIKV infection increased the infection rate of Mayaro virus (MAYV) in Ae. aegypti (Brustolin et al., 2023).In natural settings, mosquitoes are frequently coinfected with multiple arboviruses, and human coinfections have also been increasingly reported. The complex dynamics of coinfection and cotransmission pose significant challenges to public health, particularly in regions where multiple arboviruses co-circulate, potentially increasing the incidence and severity of outbreaks. Understanding the dynamics of coinfections and their implications for the vector competence of Ae. aegypti is crucial for understanding arbovirus transmission and for guiding vector surveillance and control strategies, particularly in endemic regions where multiple arboviruses coexist. In Brazil, surveillance methods such as the Rapid Index Survey for Ae. aegypti (LIRAa/LIA) are used to estimate vector infestation and outbreak risk; however, these tools do not assess mosquito coinfections (Vogels et al., 2019; Teixeira et al., 2021).In this study, we experimentally coinfected Ae. aegypti with CHIKV and two dengue virus serotypes (DENV-1 and DENV-2…

title_original: The consequence of simultaneous and sequential coinfections of Aedes aegypti with DENV-1, DENV-2, and CHIKV on vector competence

analysis.research_question_and_background: This study aimed to investigate the effects of simultaneous coinfection with CHIKV and two DENV serotypes (DENV-1 and DENV-2) on the vector competence of Aedes aegypti mosquitoes, addressing the knowledge gap regarding how co-infections might influence viral transmission dynamics in tropical regions.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study involved experimental infections of three to five-day-old female Aedes aegypti mosquitoes divided into five groups (n = 200 per group) for simultaneous coinfection and four groups (n = 300 per group) for sequential coinfection. Mosquitoes were reared under standard insectary conditions and infected by membrane feeding.
analysis.methods: Mosquitoes were infected by membrane feeding using fresh blood from BALB/c mice. Viral RNA quantification was performed using RT-qPCR, and saliva samples were collected for transmission efficiency assessment. Statistical analyses included the Kruskal–Wallis test and Shapiro–Wilk test for normality.
analysis.main_results: At 7 dpi, DENV-1 infection rates and viral loads were significantly reduced in the CD1 group compared with monoinfections, while DENV-2 showed increased viral loads in saliva. No significant differences in viral loads were detected at any time point for sequential coinfections. CHIKV infection rates were significantly lower at 14 dpi in the monoinfected group compared to the DENV-1/CHIKV coinfection group.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted that DENV-1 and DENV-2 exhibited different transmission dynamics when co-infected with CHIKV, with DENV-1 showing reduced infection rates and viral loads, and DENV-2 showing increased viral loads in saliva. This finding highlights the complex interactions between arboviruses in mosquitoes.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These results can inform surveillance strategies and risk assessments for dengue and chikungunya co-infections, as they demonstrate how viral interactions may affect transmission efficiency and vector competence in Aedes aegypti.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study had three independent biological experiments, and inter-experiment variability was assessed, but no significant differences were detected, which may limit the confidence in the results. The evidence is moderate due to the controlled experimental setting and the use of statistical tests.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the effects of simultaneous and sequential coinfections of Aedes aegypti with DENV-1, DENV-2, and CHIKV on vector competence. The research aimed to understand how co-infections might influence viral transmission dynamics in tropical regions. Mosquitoes were infected by membrane feeding using fresh blood from BALB/c mice, and viral RNA was quantified using RT-qPCR. Results showed that DENV-1 infection rates and viral loads were significantly reduced in the CD1 group compared with monoinfections, while DENV-2 showed increased viral loads in saliva. No significant differences in viral loads were detected at any time point for sequential coinfections. CHIKV infection rates were significantly lower at 14 dpi in the monoinfected group compared to the DENV-1/CHIKV coinfection group. The findings suggest that DENV-1 and DENV-2 exhibit different transmission dynamics when co-infected with CHIKV, which could inform surveillance and risk assessment strategies for dengue and chikungunya co-infections. However, the study's evidence is moderate due to its controlled experimental setting and the lack of significant differences among independent experiments.
